text.p: Australian gas and oil producer Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Wednesday it expected to carry out a shutdown of production from its Wanaea-Cossack field off Western Australia within the next 18 months.

"Some time in the next 12 to 18 months we would expect to see the installation shut down and upgraded," Woodside managing director John Akehurst said. Akehurst said Woodside was considering a shutdown of up to one month and could use the opportunity to increase oil capacity from 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) at present to as much as 140,000 bpd.
Woodside has had ongoing problems with production from the North West Shelf fields since starting operations there in late 1995. The problems have centred on the natural gas side of the operation.

"The wells will probaly produce quite comfortably about 140,000 bpd at the moment. Whether or not the sort of changes we can make to the installation will match that or not...that's really what the engineers are working on at the moment," Akehurst told reporters.
Akehurst said the options were for a shorter, earlier shutdown to fix the existing problems this year, or a longer shutdown and an increase in capacity in 1998.

"If we found that by waiting until next year we could make a more substantial upgrade, because of long lead delivery items, and we weren't hurting too badly on production this year, then we would defer it," he said.

"If we see that production this year is well below what we ought to be making and could expect to (benefit) by a shorter and earlier shutdown then we will go for the earlier option. So it's really in the balance at the moment."

Equal partners in the North West Shelf are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
